page: Microsoft Azure D2ds_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DDSv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB per core, and comes bundled with 77 GB of local SSD storage. The CPU features a 35 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI.

Performance benchmarks indicate moderate single-core capabilities but limited multi-core and memory throughput. Single-core tests, such as stress-ng and Geekbench, place the processor in the average tier, supported by solid single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression rates. However, multi-core performance in Geekbench and stress-ng falls into the lower tier, reflecting the physical single-core limitation. Memory bandwidth tests for both cached and uncached read/write operations show lower-tier throughput, and database operations or Redis SET benchmarks also register in the bottom tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D2ds_v4 offers a balanced resource profile for entry-level workloads without the premium cost of high-density memory or compute-optimized tiers. The inclusion of local SSD storage provides a cost-effective option for workloads requiring temporary storage. Due to its performance profile, this server is best suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, single-threaded applications, development environments, and low-traffic utility services that do not demand high multi-core scaling or intensive memory bandwidth.
